title: MonitorResource
description: One monitor in full: the fields `GET /v1/monitors` returns for it, plus the query and rules that define it. Every field is required; one that can be absent comes back as an explicit null.

name.description: Name of the monitor, unique within its workspace.

description.description: Monitor description. Null when no description is configured.

disabled.description: Whether the monitor is currently disabled, either by a user or automatically by the system on exceeding its alert rate or cost limit.

monitorVersion.description: Version of the monitor's current definition, as a Unix nanosecond timestamp — currently identical to `updatedAt`, and so it advances on every save. Alerts record the version they were evaluated against, so this identifies which definition produced a given alert. Carried as a string because it exceeds the JSON safe-integer range.

disabledDetail.description: Why the monitor is disabled. Null when it is enabled.

scheduled.description: Whether the monitor runs on a cron, i.e. `scheduling.cron` is set.

governorState.description: Cost-governor state. Null when no spend limit is configured for the monitor, which is the common case. `health` already folds this in; read it directly only to distinguish "no limit" from `Normal`.

aiTriagingMode.description: Whether AI auto-investigation runs when this monitor alerts. Null when the stored mode is not one this API declares. Not reported as `None`, because the filter compares the stored value and `aiTriagingMode == "None"` would not select these rows.

mutedUntil.description: When the mute covering this monitor expires. Null when the monitor is not muted, or is muted indefinitely — use `muteState` to tell those apart.

muteCount.description: Number of mute rules currently covering this monitor.

lastErrorTime.description: When the monitor last logged a fatal error. Null if it never has.

lastAlarmTime.description: When the monitor last raised an alert. Null if it never has.

lastWarnTime.description: When the monitor last logged a non-fatal warning. Null if it never has.

managedBy.description: App that manages this monitor, or null when it is user-managed. Returned id-only; request the app separately for its metadata.

lookbackSeconds.description: Window of data each evaluation considers, in seconds.

dataStabilizationDelaySeconds.description: How long evaluation waits for late data before judging a window, in seconds. Null when the monitor takes the server default.

maxAlertsPerHour.description: Alerts per hour after which the monitor disables itself. Null when the monitor takes the server default.

valueColumn.description: Column of the query output the monitor watches. Null for `Count`, `Promote` and `Composite`.

aggregation.description: How `valueColumn` is reduced over each window before the rules compare it. Null unless `ruleKind` is `Threshold`.

baseline.description: What an anomaly monitor compares `valueColumn` against. Null unless `ruleKind` is `Anomaly`. A composite's constituents and condition are read from `GET /v1/composite-monitors/{id}`.

rules.description: When the monitor alerts, one rule per severity, including a `NoData` rule when the monitor alerts on missing data. Empty for `Composite` monitors, whose condition and level are read from `GET /v1/composite-monitors/{id}`.

groupBy.description: Dimensions the rules are evaluated per; each distinct combination of values alerts independently. Empty for a single global alert.

serviceBindings.description: The service the monitor's alerts are attributed to. At most one entry; empty when the monitor is not bound to a service.

actions.description: The actions this monitor notifies through, and when each fires. Empty when it notifies nothing.

customVariables.description: Free-form values the monitor author defined for substitution into action templates. Null when there are none.

DatasetBrief.title: DatasetBrief
DatasetBrief.description: Brief record fields for a DatasetRef (label, description, iconUrl, contentType). Field naming mirrors ObjectBrief in this same file (iconUrl, not icon) for consistency across reference-brief pairs.

contentType.description:
The type of data the referenced dataset contains — Resource, Log,
Metric, OTelSpan, OTelTrace, or Unknown. Derived from the dataset's
kind and interface bindings.

DatasetContentType.title: DatasetContentType
DatasetContentType.description:
The type of data a dataset contains. For Resource datasets, this is
determined by the dataset kind. For other kinds, it is derived from the
dataset's interface bindings. Returns Unknown if no recognized interface
is found.

DatasetRef.title: DatasetRef
DatasetRef.description: A reference to a dataset. Always carries the id; the optional `record` field carries the brief metadata, populated when expand=true. Mirrors ObjectRef (see ObjectRef / ObjectBrief in this file).

Monitor-ActionRule.title: MonitorActionRule
Monitor-ActionRule.description: Binds one action to the monitor, and says when it fires.

levels.description: Severities that fire this action. Empty means every severity.

conditions.description: Condition on the alert's values, so one monitor can route different groups to different actions. Null to fire for every alert at `levels`.

sendEndNotifications.description: Whether the action also fires when an alert resolves.

sendRemindersIntervalSeconds.description: How often to re-notify while an alert stays open, in seconds. Null to notify once.

Monitor-AiTriagingMode.title: MonitorAiTriagingMode
Monitor-AiTriagingMode.description: Whether AI auto-investigation runs when this monitor alerts. `None` disables it; `Triage` runs it.

Monitor-AlarmLevel.title: MonitorAlarmLevel
Monitor-AlarmLevel.description: Severity of an alert. `NoData` comes from a no-data rule rather than a comparison.

Monitor-AlarmMode.title: MonitorAlarmMode
Monitor-AlarmMode.description: How alerts span consecutive cron runs. `PerRun` raises a separate alert per firing run. `Ongoing` extends one alert across consecutive runs that fire for the same group and severity.

Monitor-AlertState.title: MonitorAlertState
Monitor-AlertState.description: Whether the monitor is alerting now, has alerted before, or never has. `Triggering` means an alarm is open, or one was raised since the last evaluation; a monitor that is turned off is never `Triggering` because it cannot evaluate. `Previous` means it has alerted at some point but is not now — the same set as `lastAlarmTime != null` minus the triggering ones.

Monitor-Baseline.title: MonitorBaseline
Monitor-Baseline.description: The baseline an anomaly monitor compares `valueColumn` against, and how far a value must stray from it. Exactly one of `basicAlgorithm` and `seasonalAlgorithm` is set.

computationWindowSeconds.description: How much history the baseline is computed over, in seconds. Null when the monitor takes the server default.

frequencySeconds.description: How often the baseline is recomputed, in seconds. Null when the monitor takes the server default.

basicAlgorithm.description: Set when the monitor uses the standard-deviation algorithm.

seasonalAlgorithm.description: Set when the monitor uses the seasonal algorithm.

Monitor-BasicAlgorithm.title: MonitorBasicAlgorithm
Monitor-BasicAlgorithm.description: Baseline as a mean, with anomalies a number of standard deviations away.

numStandardDeviations.description: How many standard deviations from the mean count as anomalous.

Monitor-BooleanOperator.title: MonitorBooleanOperator
Monitor-BooleanOperator.description: How a set of conditions combine.

Monitor-BoundComparisonFunction.title: MonitorBoundComparisonFunction
Monitor-BoundComparisonFunction.description: Which side of the baseline counts as anomalous.

Monitor-ColumnFilter.title: MonitorColumnFilter
Monitor-ColumnFilter.description: A test on one column: its `columnComparisons`, combined by `operator`. The column is named as in `groupBy`: exactly one of `column`, `link` and `tag`.

column.description: A column of the query output. Null for a link or tag.

path.description: Dotted path into `column`. Null for the whole column.

link.description: A link column. Null unless comparing on a link.

tag.description: Correlation tag, without the `#`. Null unless comparing on a tag.

operator.description: How `columnComparisons` combine: `Or` matches when any holds, `And` when all do. Always returned. A monitor saved without one gets `And` when any comparison is `NotEqual`, `NotContains`, `NotStartsWith` or `IsNotNull`, and `Or` otherwise.

columnComparisons.description: Comparisons applied to the column's value.

Monitor-ColumnPath.title: MonitorColumnPath
Monitor-ColumnPath.description: A column, optionally a field within it.

name.description: The column's name within its dataset.

path.description: Dotted path into the column. Null for the whole column.

Monitor-Comparison.title: MonitorComparison
Monitor-Comparison.description: One comparison applied to a value.

compareValue.description:
The right-hand side as a string, in the form `valueType` names. Null
for `IsNull` and `IsNotNull`, and for a stored null.

Numbers are base-10, booleans `true`/`false`, timestamps RFC 3339 in
UTC, and **durations a count of nanoseconds** -- the one place in this
schema a duration is not in seconds.

valueType.description: Type of `compareValue`. Null when the comparison has no operand (`IsNull`, `IsNotNull`).

Monitor-ComparisonExpression.title: MonitorComparisonExpression
Monitor-ComparisonExpression.description: Boolean tree over column comparisons: `operator` combines this node's `compareTerms` and `subExpressions`.

subExpressions.description: Nested expressions. Empty at a leaf.

Monitor-ComparisonFunction.title: MonitorComparisonFunction
Monitor-ComparisonFunction.description: How a value is compared. `IsNull` and `IsNotNull` take no right-hand side; the rest require one.

Monitor-ComparisonTerm.title: MonitorComparisonTerm
Monitor-ComparisonTerm.description: One comparison against one column, named as in `groupBy`: exactly one of `column`, `link` and `tag`.

column.description: A column of the query output. Null for a link or tag.

path.description: Dotted path into `column`. Null for the whole column.

link.description: A link column. Null unless comparing on a link.

tag.description: Correlation tag, without the `#`. Null unless comparing on a tag.

rawCron.description: Crontab expression for when to evaluate.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the cron is interpreted in.

Monitor-DisabledByAlertRateLimit.title: MonitorDisabledByAlertRateLimit
Monitor-DisabledByAlertRateLimit.description: Detail for a monitor disabled for exceeding its alert rate limit.

alertRateLimit.description: The monitor's configured maximum alerts per hour.

alertsGenerated.description: Alerts generated within the lookback window, which exceeded `alertRateLimit` and triggered the disable.

lookbackSeconds.description: Length of the window over which alerts were counted.

Monitor-DisabledByCost.title: MonitorDisabledByCost
Monitor-DisabledByCost.description: Detail for a monitor the cost governor disabled.

creditLimitPerDay.description: The daily credit limit the monitor exceeded.

Monitor-DisabledByResultTooBig.title: MonitorDisabledByResultTooBig
Monitor-DisabledByResultTooBig.description: Detail for a monitor disabled because a run result was too large. Either the bytes pair or the rows pair is set; the other is null.

bytesRead.description: Bytes read. Null for a row-limit disable.

bytesLimit.description: Byte limit exceeded. Null for a row-limit disable.

rowsRead.description: Rows read. Null for a byte-limit disable.

rowsLimit.description: Row limit exceeded. Null for a byte-limit disable.

Monitor-DisabledByUser.title: MonitorDisabledByUser
Monitor-DisabledByUser.description: Detail for a monitor a user explicitly disabled.

Monitor-DisabledDetail.title: MonitorDisabledDetail
Monitor-DisabledDetail.description: Why the monitor is disabled. Exactly one of the cause-specific fields is populated, matching `cause`; the others are null.

Monitor-GovernorState.title: MonitorGovernorState
Monitor-GovernorState.description: Where the monitor sits against its configured spend limit. `Normal` is within budget, `GracePeriod` is over it but still evaluating, and `CostDisabled` means the limit has turned it off.

Monitor-Grouping.title: MonitorGrouping
Monitor-Grouping.description: One dimension the rules are evaluated per. Exactly one of `column`, `link` and `tag` is set; `path` only accompanies `column`.

column.description: A column of the query output. Null for a link or tag.

path.description: Dotted path into `column`. Null for the whole column.

link.description: A link column, grouping by the linked resource. Null otherwise.

tag.description: Correlation tag, without the `#`. Null otherwise.

meta.description: What `link` or `tag` resolved to when the monitor was saved. Read-only. Null for a plain `column`.

Monitor-GroupingMeta.title: MonitorGroupingMeta
Monitor-GroupingMeta.description: The physical columns a link or correlation tag resolves to.

srcFields.description: Columns of this dataset the link or tag reads.

dstFields.description: Columns of the target dataset a link resolves to. Empty for a tag.

targetDataset.description: Dataset a link points at. Null for a tag.

Monitor-Health.title: MonitorHealth
Monitor-Health.description:
The monitor's operating state as one value, which is what the monitors
list shows in its Health column and facets on.

`rollupStatus` answers a narrower question — how the last evaluation
went — so it reports `Running` for a monitor that is turned off, over its
spend limit, or on a passive cluster. `health` ranks those causes above
the run outcome, highest first:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CostDisabled` | Turned off after exceeding its spend limit. |
| `AlertRateLimitDisabled` | Turned off after exceeding its alert rate. |
| `Disabled` | Turned off by a user. |
| `ClusterPassive` | Its customer's monitoring is not active on this cluster, so nothing evaluates. Set for every monitor of that customer at once. |
| `AtRisk` | Inside the grace period before its spend limit disables it. |
| `Failed` | An error was logged since the last run, less than a week ago. |
| `Warnings` | Likewise a warning. |
| `Initializing` | An anomaly monitor that has not yet produced its output dataset, so it cannot evaluate. |
| `Running` | None of the above. |

A monitor can satisfy several; only the highest is reported, and the
ranking may change. `Initializing` is only partially reachable — see the
note under the list operation's `filter` for the warm-up tail this
endpoint cannot see.

Monitor-InputRole.title: MonitorInputRole
Monitor-InputRole.description: How a stage uses an input: `Data` is queried, `Reference` is only joined against.

intervalSeconds.description: How often the monitor evaluates, in seconds.

Monitor-MultiStageQuery.title: MonitorMultiStageQuery
Monitor-MultiStageQuery.description: The OPAL query the rules are evaluated over, as a pipeline of stages.

outputStage.description: `id` of the stage the rules read.

Monitor-MuteState.title: MonitorMuteState
Monitor-MuteState.description: Whether mute rules currently suppress this monitor's notifications. `PartiallyMuted` means every covering rule is scoped to particular alert groupings, so some alerts still notify.

Monitor-RollupStatus.title: MonitorRollupStatus
Monitor-RollupStatus.description: Single health summary, derived from the monitor's other fields and resolved by priority, highest first: `Disabled` (by a user or a limit), `Failed` (an error logged since the last run and less than a week old), `Warnings` (likewise a warning), `Initializing` (an anomaly monitor that has not yet produced its output dataset, so it cannot evaluate yet), `Running` (the default). A monitor can satisfy more than one — only the highest is reported, and the ranking may change. See the note under the list operation's `filter` for the part of `Initializing` this endpoint cannot see.

Monitor-Rule.title: MonitorRule
Monitor-Rule.description:
One alert condition at one severity: the monitor triggers an alert at `level` when every entry in `triggerComparisons` holds, for the groups (or rows) every entry in the filters matches. `ruleKind` decides which fields are used; the lists it does not use are empty:
| Rule | Fields used | |---|---| | `Count`, `Threshold`, `Anomaly` | `triggerComparisons`, `groupFilters` | | `Promote` | `rowFilters` | | `level: NoData` | `expirationSeconds` (`Threshold` only) |
A `NoData` rule alerts when no data arrives for a full lookback window. Only `Threshold` and `Anomaly` monitors have one, at most one each, and it watches the same `valueColumn` as the other rules.

triggerComparisons.description:
Comparisons that trigger the alert, all of which must hold (so two
entries express a range). What they compare depends on `ruleKind`:

| `ruleKind` | Compared value |
|---|---|
| `Count` | Number of rows in each group over the window |
| `Threshold` | `valueColumn`, reduced over the window by `aggregation` |
| `Anomaly` | Percentage (0-100) of the window outside `baseline` |

groupFilters.description: Restricts the rule to groups matching every entry. Each entry tests one of the `groupBy` columns. Empty when the rule applies to every group.

rowFilters.description: Rows of the query output to promote to an alert at this level: a row is promoted when it matches every entry. Empty promotes every row.

expirationSeconds.description: How long a no-data alert stays open before resolving itself, in seconds. Set only on a `Threshold` monitor's `NoData` rule, where null means the server default. Always null otherwise, including for `Anomaly`, whose no-data alerts always close after a fixed time.

Monitor-RuleKind.title: MonitorRuleKind
Monitor-RuleKind.description: The evaluation rule kind of the monitor. `Composite` is the one kind that inspects no query: it alerts on a boolean condition over whether other monitors are currently alerting, correlated per group.

Monitor-Scheduling.title: MonitorScheduling
Monitor-Scheduling.description: When the monitor evaluates. `automatic` is always returned, `true` or `false`. Alongside it, one of `interval`, `transform` and `cron` is set: the schedule the monitor actually runs on, with the server's defaults filled in. All three are null only for a monitor that is saved but not yet running and asked for no schedule; the server picks one when it starts the monitor.

automatic.description: Whether the server chose this schedule, rather than the monitor setting one. An automatic schedule is re-chosen whenever the monitor is saved, so it follows changes to the query and lookback. Always `true` for `Anomaly` and `Composite` monitors, which cannot set one.

interval.description: Evaluation on a fixed interval. Chosen by the server, not requested: anomaly and composite monitors always run this way, as does a monitor whose query cannot be accelerated.

transform.description: Evaluation each time the input dataset's transform runs.

Monitor-SeasonalAlgorithm.title: MonitorSeasonalAlgorithm
Monitor-SeasonalAlgorithm.description: Baseline that models daily and weekly cycles, so a regular nightly trough is not read as an anomaly.

sensitivity.description: How readily a departure from the baseline alerts. Null when the monitor takes the server default.

dailyPeriods.description: Daily cycles the model fits. Null when the monitor takes the server default.

weeklyPeriods.description: Weekly cycles the model fits. Null when the monitor takes the server default.

Monitor-SeasonalSensitivity.title: MonitorSeasonalSensitivity
Monitor-SeasonalSensitivity.description: How readily a departure from a seasonal baseline alerts, from `Low` (fewest alerts) to `VeryHigh`.

Monitor-ServiceBinding.title: MonitorServiceBinding
Monitor-ServiceBinding.description: A service a monitor's alerts are attributed to, as its three identifying dimensions.

Monitor-ServiceBindingMatchMode.title: MonitorServiceBindingMatchMode
Monitor-ServiceBindingMatchMode.description: How a binding dimension is matched. `Exact` matches `value`. `Wildcard` takes each alert's value from the monitor's `groupBy` columns or the input dataset's correlation tags.

Monitor-ServiceBindingValue.title: MonitorServiceBindingValue
Monitor-ServiceBindingValue.description: One dimension of a service binding.

value.description: The value this dimension matches. Null when `matchMode` is `Wildcard`.

Monitor-StageInput.title: MonitorStageInput
Monitor-StageInput.description: One source a stage reads: a dataset (by `dataset` or `datasetPath`), an earlier stage, or a parameter. The fields it does not use are null.

inputName.description: The `@name` OPAL refers to this input by, without the `@`.

dataset.description: Dataset this input reads. Null when it reads something else.

datasetPath.description: The dataset as `Workspace.path/Name`, when it was saved that way. Null otherwise.

stageId.description: `id` of an earlier stage of this query. Null when not reading a stage.

parameterId.description: Parameter the dataset is taken from. Null when not reading a parameter.

Monitor-StageQuery.title: MonitorStageQuery
Monitor-StageQuery.description: One stage of a monitor's input query.

id.description: Identifies the stage within this query. `outputStage` and other stages' `input[].stageId` refer to it by this value.

Monitor-TransformSchedule.title: MonitorTransformSchedule
Monitor-TransformSchedule.description: Evaluation driven by the input dataset's transform.

freshnessGoalSeconds.description: How stale the monitor's data may get, in seconds.

Monitor-ValueAggregation.title: MonitorValueAggregation
Monitor-ValueAggregation.description: How the values in a window are reduced before comparison: `Max`, `Min`, `AvgOf` and `SumOf` compare the largest, smallest, mean or total. The older `AllOf` and `AnyOf` require every or at least one value to match; new monitors use `Min` or `Max` instead.

Monitor-ValueType.title: MonitorValueType
Monitor-ValueType.description: The type of a comparison's right-hand side.

MonitorAction-Brief.title: MonitorActionBrief
MonitorAction-Brief.description: A bound action, with enough of its configuration to read it back and send it again.

label.description: The action's name. An inline action's is generated rather than chosen. Null when the action has none.

inline.description: Whether the action belongs to this monitor alone rather than being shared.

email.description: The email payload. Set when `type` is `Email`.

webhook.description: The webhook payload. Set when `type` is `Webhook`, `Slack` or `PagerDuty`, all of which post a webhook.

subject.description: Subject template. Null when the action sets none.

body.description: Body template. Null when the action sets none.

fragments.description: Named template fragments the subject and body can include. Null when the action defines none.

MonitorAction-HttpMethod.title: MonitorActionHttpMethod
MonitorAction-HttpMethod.description: HTTP method a webhook action posts with.

MonitorAction-Ref.title: MonitorActionRef
MonitorAction-Ref.description: Reference to a monitor action; `record` is populated only with `expand=true`. Actions have no endpoint of their own yet, so read one through a monitor that binds it.

MonitorAction-Type.title: MonitorActionType
MonitorAction-Type.description: How an action notifies. `PagerDuty` and `Slack` are webhooks posted to those services.

MonitorAction-Webhook.title: MonitorActionWebhook
MonitorAction-Webhook.description: A webhook notification's payload, also used for PagerDuty and Slack. A PagerDuty routing key is part of the `body` template, not a field of its own.

url.description: Endpoint to post to. Null when the action sets none.

method.description: HTTP method. Null when the action sets none.

body.description: Request-body template. Null when the action sets none.

fragments.description: Named template fragments the body can include. Null when the action defines none.

ObjectBrief.title: ObjectBrief
ObjectBrief.description: Brief record fields for an ObjectRef. This type is polymorphic: additional fields pointing to specific object types (e.g. dataset, dashboard, monitor) may be added in the future as needed.

managedBy.description: Owner/manager of this object. Always returned as an id-only ObjectRef even when the parent was requested with expand=true: `expand` populates a single layer of brief data, so `record.managedBy` on a brief is itself never expanded. Pass the inner id back through a separate request (or filter via CEL, which lazily resolves) to access the manager's brief.

ObjectRef.title: ObjectRef
ObjectRef.description: A reference to another resource. Always carries the id; the optional `record` field carries the brief metadata, populated when expand=true. Brief expansion applies to one layer only — fields inside `record` that are themselves ObjectRefs (e.g. `record.managedBy`) are returned id-only, never with their own `record` populated. CEL filter expressions can deeper-resolve via lazy wrapper resolution if needed.
